title: Coefficient four with a complete single-file proof and explicit all-length remainder

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total certificate-prefix language defined by the exact evaluator in proof.md Part A: at actual length N choose the least prime k>=B, where B is the least positive integer with B^5>32*N^3; test the k-bit monic-polynomial prefix by the prime-degree irreducibility test; on a valid prefix apply the specified descending-power BK symmetric polynomial and constant-coefficient functional to the zero-padded N-k payload. The specified small-length and invalid-prefix branches return zero. One fixed polynomial-time evaluator and empty-witness NP verifier define all lengths.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total language in P, hence NP, every exact full-B2 circuit at actual input length N has at least 4N-52*N^(4/5) gates for every integer N>=2^20. In particular liminf over all integer N of C_B2(F_N)/N>=4, with the all-length epsilon thresholds proved in proof.md Part D.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}
